title: Local block normal form for a nonempty open subscheme
statement: Let the hypotheses of lem-pc-constant-rank-map-local-normal-form hold, and assume in addition that Z is nonempty. Then for every z in Z there are an open neighbourhood U of z and isomorphisms eS and eT of the restricted finite free modules with the (m-a) plus a and a plus (n-a) biproducts, respectively, such that the restricted map is eS.hom followed by the projection to the second source summand, the inclusion of the first target summand, and eT.inv.

source.place: normal-form claim and local kernel/image splitting

proof.text: On an affine neighbourhood of any point of Z, use the field-valued points in hrank and invariance of matrix rank under residue-field extension to see that every residue-field matrix has rank a.

All (a+1)-minors vanish modulo every prime and hence vanish in the reduced affine ring. At the chosen point a nonzero a-minor exists; after shrinking to its principal open it is invertible. Permuting rows and columns and applying invertible block operations gives diag(I_a,0), since the Schur-complement entries are (a+1)-minors divided by the pivot determinant.
Reorder the resulting free bases and transport them through restriction and pullback to obtain the displayed biproduct factorization. The empty minor handles a=0.

proof_origin.place: Proof (3), normal-form claim; existing lem-pc-constant-rank-map-kernel-image proof steps 1 and 2

mathlib_searches.query: A constant rank matrix over a reduced ring is locally equivalent to an identity block and a zero block
A constant rank matrix over a reduced ring is locally equivalent to a block identity matrix and its kernel and image are locally free
mathlib_searches.verdict: No reduced-ring local normal form; division-ring and rank-condition results only.
The last theorem requires a square matrix over a field; not this reduced-ring, rectangular local statement.

mathlib_searches.results: Generic free-locus, flat-rank, rank-nullity and Picard-group results; no local constant rank block form over a reduced ring.

from.place: Proof (3): over a reduced base a map of finite free modules of locally constant fibre rank has locally the normal form diag(I,0)

theorem exists_local_normal_form_of_constantRank_nonempty
    {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Y] [Nonempty Z] {M N : Y.Modules} {m n : ℕ}
    (eM : M ≅ free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)))
    (eN : N ≅ free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))
    (φ : M ⟶ N) (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (a : ℕ)
    (hrank : ∀ z : Z, ∃ (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (_ : IsField R) (g : Spec R ⟶ Y),
      Set.range g.base = {j.base z} ∧
      ((freeMatrix (eM.inv ≫ φ ≫ eN.hom)).map g.appTop).rank = a) :
    ∀ z : Z, ∃ U : Z.Opens, z ∈ U ∧
      ∃ (eS : ((Modules.pullback j).obj M).restrict U.ι ≅
          free (ULift.{u} (Fin (m - a))) ⊞ free (ULift.{u} (Fin a)))
        (eT : ((Modules.pullback j).obj N).restrict U.ι ≅
          free (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) ⊞ free (ULift.{u} (Fin (n - a)))),
        (restrictFunctor U.ι).map ((Modules.pullback j).map φ) =
          eS.hom ≫ biprod.snd ≫ biprod.inl ≫ eT.inv
